config.title: Reusable Button

intro.title: Reusable Button
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Button component in React with TypeScript. You will learn how to create a component that accepts props to customize its appearance and behavior, such as text and click actions. The core concept is component reusability, which allows you to write flexible and maintainable code. You'll use TypeScript interfaces to define the component's props, ensuring type safety. This lesson covers basic React component structure and event handling, perfect for beginners starting with React and TypeScript.
intro.usecase: Reusable buttons are foundational components in every modern web application. You'll find them in e-commerce checkout flows, dashboard action panels, form submissions, and navigation menus across platforms like Shopify, Notion, and GitHub. As a developer, you'll build button components once and reuse them throughout your application, ensuring consistent styling and behavior while reducing code duplication. This pattern is essential for maintaining scalable, maintainable UI systems in production applications.

objectives: Construct a reusable Button component with TypeScript interfaces for props
Initialize and configure component state to manage button interactions
Implement conditional rendering for different button variants (primary, secondary)
Bind event handlers to control button click behavior
Apply TypeScript type safety to component props and event parameters
Integrate the reusable Button component into a parent application
Manipulate component styling based on props and state changes

steps.title: Create ButtonProps interface

steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Make sure to include label (string), onClick (() => void), and optional disabled (boolean).

steps.expectedOutcome: A Button functional component is defined with typed props.
successCriteria: Button component is created and accepts ButtonProps.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named Button and accepts ButtonProps.
